sentences.text: Scientists estimated this tiny dinosaur measured about one meter in total length and weighed roughly six kilograms.
Its slender upper arm bones, which were only four centimeters long, along with a bowed thighbone, suggest it was facultatively bipedal.
A unique trait of its skull is that the premaxilla bone carries just one tooth.
The outer wall of the dentary bone is notably thickened and features a pattern of anastomosing grooves and ridges.
The name Xuanhuasaurus niei was originally published in 1985 but was invalid because it lacked a description and a specified holotype.
At one meter long and six kilograms, it represents one of the smallest known ceratopsians.
Fossils were discovered in the Houcheng Formation in Hebei Province, northeastern China, starting with a fragmentary skeleton found in the 1970s by Nie Rongzhen near Yanjiagou.
Three additional fossil specimens were discovered in the summer of 2003.
The genus Xuanhuaceratops was formally named by Zhao and colleagues in 2006.
Researchers believe the holotype specimen was likely a fully grown adult.
Xuanhuaceratops belongs to the family Chaoyangsauridae and is considered one of the earliest ceratopsians.
In 2006, it was classified within Chaoyangsauridae, a clade identified as a basal lineage of Ceratopsia for all neoceratopsians and psittacosaurids.
The animal belongs to the class Ornithischia.
Xuanhuaceratops lived during the Late Jurassic Period, specifically the Tithonian stage between 150.8 and 145.5 million years ago, in Asia.
